headline: OpenAI 澄清 Pro 套餐无 5 小时限制，Karpathy 用 Claude Code 三分钟做出视频站
bullets: OpenAI 的 thsottiaux 澄清所有 Pro 套餐都没有 5 小时限制，Pro 100/200/500 分别是 Plus 用量的 10/20/50 倍，还在问要不要出 Pro 50。
Karpathy 用 Claude Code 三分钟一次性做出 TristanTube，收录 4.7 万个硬核视频，还带电视模式。
Levie 说 AI 编程的生产力提升能到 AI 前的 10 到 100 倍，而且这个差距没在缩小，反而越滚越大。
Levie 还认为 agent 的推理可以放到远处数据中心跑，因为长任务对延迟不敏感，经济价值又高。
builder 们在聊数据中心建设变难会让现有算力持有者（hyperscaler）赢，代价是新模型训练速度被拖慢。
sentiment: 整体偏兴奋和观望：兴奋的是 agent 和 AI 编程带来的夸张杠杆，观望的是算力、政策和数据中心这些外部约束会不会卡住进度。

posts.name: Nikunj Kothari
posts.text:
ok here’s how we get investors to fomo our series A and get seven term sheets..

first, we have to vague post revenue. or customers. this is absolutely critical. no y axis, just keep showing numbers and to the right. graphs work and of course get your investors to quote tweet it and take credit. they love doing that anyway. make it vague like “slowly but surely” or “i see an exponential when I see one”

ok, once you do that, you know you can do another launch video for features or even better multiple for features so you get maximum airtime. after that case studies are critical - get a trendsetter company to talk about you or even better have the labs mention you in articles. this will guarantee cold emails to grab coffee from partners. 

also you know you can buy “articles” in “premier” publications. you can even run ads against it targeted to just investors too. you’re joking? no dead serious bro. 

ok now that you have interest and top of mindshare - the most important thing is to use the magic mantras of “large ambition” and combinations of “long horizon agent swarms abilterared world models physical ai”. 

and finally and most importantly you don’t have a deck because of course we’re not raising, we were thinking early next year. and of course we still got pre empted so we don’t have a data room even. you get on or not it’s your call. 

and then you use the magic words of optimizing for the best partner but let’s be honest we both know i just want the best valuation. 

(again the whole thing is satire, but individually each line is true)
posts.summaryZh: 他反讽融资套路：发模糊的收入或客户图、不给 y 轴、让投资人转发邀功、多发功能发布视频、买“顶级媒体”文章，就能拿到七份 term sheet。

posts.name: Aaron Levie
posts.text:
This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI. 

With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding.  

What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems.

Right now this is most pronounced in software engineering for the obvious reasons. But there’s no reason we don’t start to see this in a number of other computer-use-sensitive domains like other scientific fields, AEC, finance, cyber, and more. Going to get quite wild.
posts.summaryZh: 他说现在不少例子里 AI 编程产出比 AI 前高 10 到 100 倍，前提是工具链对、懂领域、代码库较新、会同时用多个 agent；而且这个差距没在缩小，反而在扩大。

posts.name: Zara Zhang
posts.text:
So many people speak of startup as if their fates are predestined: X idea will never work out; the market for Y is too niche...

But startups' fates are MADE, not predetermined. Given one idea, there are 1000 ways to execute it, 100 people will have 100 different approaches. Brilliant people with brilliant execution often create something when there was nothing, or make the impossible seem obvious in hindsight.
posts.summaryZh: 她认为创业成败不是命中注定的，同一个点子有上千种执行方式，牛人靠执行能把不可能变成事后看来理所当然。

posts.name: Aaron Levie
posts.text:
The interesting thing about AI agents is that as a theoretical matter, their inference can kind of run anywhere. AI is one of the few areas of technology that isn’t *as* sensitive to latency back to the user. 

Long running agents are now going to be the norm, which means it’s ok to send off work to an AI factory somewhere and that work can essentially be largely done within that remote data center and a final result spit back to the user. The data can pass into these systems in an encrypted manner, be combed through by agents, and then disregarded right after. 

And because the economic value of the task is so high relative to the latency sensitivity (eg getting back $500 in value from an automated task, but it takes an extra second to return), you don’t have to have the inference to be particularly close to the user. 

Also, because inference is a temporary process with no sensitive data needing to be stored long term where the inference is happening, you can effectively treat AI factories as ephemeral systems, changing some of the data residency dynamics slightly.

Combined, this means you have more flexibility in where you can begin to deploy AI data centers. This is both a huge economic opportunity for the states or countries (or space) that want to take advantage of this fact. And it’s a loss to the states or countries that decide to forgo the opportunity.
posts.summaryZh: 他说 agent 的推理理论上可以放在任何地方，因为长任务对延迟不敏感、任务经济价值高，数据加密进去、用完就丢，不必靠近用户。
